title: 音声大規模言語モデルにおける推論メカニズムと事後学習のフロンティア
titleEn: Frontiers of Reasoning Mechanisms and Post-Training in Audio Large Language Models
dek: 内部表現、強化学習、思考の連鎖（CoT）推論が、音声大規模言語モデルを単なる文字起こしツールからメディア編集やフォレンジック分析のための高度なエンジンへとどのように変貌させているのかを探る。
dekEn: An exploration of how internal representations, reinforcement learning, and chain-of-thought reasoning are transforming audio large language models from basic transcribers into advanced engines for media editing and forensic analysis.
summaryEn: This feature examines the intersection of reasoning mechanisms, architectural decoupling, and post-training frameworks in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs). As models transition from standardized speech recognition to complex real-world workflows such as media chapterization and audio forgery detection, novel methodologies emerge to handle their unique demands. We explore how continuous latent workspaces preserve fine-grained acoustic details, how middle-layer probes uncover language-agnostic conceptual emergence, and how policy optimization algorithms align model outputs with subjective editorial judgments. By synthesizing recent advances in decoupled representations and reinforcement learning, this review highlights both the technical trajectories and the ongoing evaluation challenges in audio AI research.
keyPointsEn: Decoupled continuous representations enable unified models to perform both long-context audio understanding and fine-grained speech generation.
Middle-layer probing reveals that audio models formulate language-agnostic concepts before text emission without explicit chain-of-thought prompts.
Post-training frameworks utilizing group relative policy optimization align LALMs with subjective editorial criteria for tasks like media chapterization.

perspectives.label: 内部表現と推論
perspectives.description: 言語的、パラ言語的、概念的な情報が音声言語モデルの中間層内でどのように抽出され、表現されているかを調査する。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Investigating how linguistic, paralinguistic, and conceptual information is extracted and represented within intermediate layers of audio language models.

perspectives.label: 事後学習とデプロイの制約
perspectives.description: メディア編集や章立てなどの現実世界の要件を満たすために、効率的なアライメントフレームワークと強化学習戦略を設計する。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Designing efficient alignment frameworks and reinforcement learning strategies to meet real-world production requirements like media editing and chapterization.

perspectives.label: 評価の限界と解釈可能性
perspectives.description: 明示的な根拠に基づく推論の監督を通じて、複雑なフォレンジックおよび編集タスクにおけるハルシネーションと透明性の欠如を克服する。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Overcoming hallucinations and lack of transparency in complex forensic and editorial tasks through explicit evidence-grounded reasoning supervision.

sections.heading: 現実世界の音声理解における課題
sections.headingEn: The Challenge of Real-World Audio Understanding

blocks.text: 長年にわたり、標準化されたベンチマークは、主に自動音声認識や単純な音声分類タスクを通じて、大規模音声言語モデルの成功を評価してきました。しかし、これらのシステムを実際のメディアワークフロー、アーカイブのインデックス作成、およびコンテンツ配信に導入すると、実験室での評価指標と実運用におけるニーズの間に大きな機能的隔たりがあることが浮き彫りになります。現実世界の音声ストリームでは、単なる文字起こしにとどまらず、モデルが連続信号を処理し、長時間の時間的文脈を把握し、さまざまな音響条件下で複雑な編集上の判断を下すことが求められます。テキストに合わせられた応答を前提とした従来の手法は、こうした環境では失敗することが少なくありません。これは、標準的な自己回帰トレーニングが隠れ状態をテキスト生成専用に形成するため、きめ細かな音声学的詳細、韻律、感情的ニュアンス、環境音イベントといった重要な音響属性を意図せず切り捨ててしまうからです。さらに、標準的な音声エンコーダーによって生成される高レートのトークンシーケンスは、重度のアテンション計算コストを発生させ、スループットの高い本番環境での拡張性を著しく制限します。こうした構造的限界に対処するには、表面的な文字起こしを超越し、複雑な音響シーンに対して頑健で多ホップな推論を実行できるアーキテクチャへと移行し、それによって生の音声知与と高水準の意味理解との間の溝を埋める必要があります。
blocks.textEn: Standardized benchmarks have long measured the success of Large Audio Language Models primarily through automated speech recognition and simple audio classification tasks. However, deploying these systems into practical media workflows, archival indexing, and content distribution exposes a profound capability gap between laboratory metrics and production needs. Real-world auditory streams demand considerably more than literal transcriptions; they require models to process continuous signals, navigate extended temporal contexts, and execute complex editorial judgments under varying acoustic conditions. Prior practices built around text-aligned responses often fail in these settings because standard autoregressive training shapes hidden states exclusively for text generation, inadvertently discarding critical acoustic attributes such as fine-grained phonetic detail, prosody, emotional affect, and ambient sound events. Furthermore, high-rate token sequences generated by standard audio encoders create heavy attention computation costs that severely limit scalability in high-throughput production environments. Addressing these structural limitations requires moving beyond surface-level transcription toward architectures capable of robust, multi-hop reasoning over complex acoustic scenes, thereby bridging the divide between raw audio perception and high-level semantic comprehension.

blocks.text: 本番環境において、下流のアプリケーションは、ユーザーの指示への継続的な適応と、多様な音響環境にわたる高い忠実度を求めています。モデルが重なり合う話し手、音響的劣化、あるいは動的なマルチチャンネルの手がかりに直面したとき、従来の単一ストリームアーキテクチャは頻繁に破綻します。このもろさは、重要な意味的文脈を失うことなく、複雑な知覚タスクを生成経路から切り離すことのできる、頑健な中間表現の早急な必要性を浮き彫りにしています。
blocks.textEn: In production contexts, downstream applications demand continuous adaptation to user instructions and high fidelity across diverse acoustic environments. When models encounter overlapping speakers, acoustic degradation, or dynamic multi-channel cues, conventional single-stream architectures frequently collapse. This brittleness emphasizes the urgent need for robust intermediate representations that can decouple complex perception tasks from generation pathways without losing critical semantic context.

sections.heading: 単一の文字起こしから統合された潜在ワークスペースへ
sections.headingEn: From Monolithic Transcription to Unified Latent Workspaces

blocks.text: 音声言語モデリングの技術的軌跡は、音声認識、音響イベント検出、および音声合成を、別個の機械学習モデルによって管理される完全に切り離された問題として扱う、孤立したパイプラインから始まりました。初期の統合の試みでは、凍結された音声エンコーダーと大規模言語モデルのバックボーンを結合し、強力な受動的知覚能力をもたらしたものの、対話的な動作は厳しく制限されていました。研究者が汎用的な音声理解を追求するにつれて、主要なアーキテクチャ上のボトルネックが浮上しました。すなわち、理解タスクではコンパクトでコンテキストの長い特徴量が強く好まれる一方で、音声生成では微細な音響詳細を保持できる高い再構築性を持つ特徴量が求められたのです。この根本的な緊張関係により、複数のエンコーダー層からより豊かな意味的証拠を抽出するように設計された、多層アグリゲーターやカスタム音声Q-Formerへの構造的シフトが促されました。より最近では、この分野は連続的な潜在ワークスペースと分離された経路を統合する統一アーキテクチャへと進化しており、モデルが、法外な自己回帰的デコードペナルティを発生させることなく、応答を生成する前に複雑な音響情報を整理できるようになっています。この進化の過程は、知覚、推論、生成という矛盾する表現の要求を、単一のトレーニング可能なフレームワーク内で調和させようとする不断の努力を浮き彫りにしています。
blocks.textEn: The technological trajectory of audio language modeling began with isolated pipelines that treated speech recognition, acoustic event detection, and synthesis as completely disjoint problems managed by separate machine learning models. Early integration efforts coupled frozen audio encoders with large language model backbones, yielding strong passive perception capabilities but heavily constrained interactive behaviors. As researchers pursued general-purpose audio understanding, a major architectural bottleneck emerged: understanding tasks heavily favored compact, long-context features, whereas speech generation required highly reconstructible features capable of preserving fine acoustic details. This fundamental tension prompted a structural shift toward multi-layer aggregators and custom audio Q-Formers designed to extract richer semantic evidence from multiple encoder layers. More recently, the field has progressed toward unified architectures that integrate continuous latent workspaces and decoupled pathways, allowing models to organize complex acoustic information prior to generating responses without incurring prohibitive autoregressive decoding penalties. This evolutionary sequence highlights a continuous effort to reconcile the conflicting representational demands of perception, reasoning, and generation within a single trainable framework.

blocks.text: 初期の世代のモデルは、自動音声認識の出力をテキストのみの大規模言語モデルに直接入力する、厳格なカスケード型パイプラインに大きく依存していました。実装は容易であるものの、この分離されたシーケンスには致命的なエラー伝播という問題があり、初期の文字起こしミスが後段の推論を永続的に破損させていました。エンドツーエンドのマルチモーダルアーキテクチャへの移行は、音響特徴量をトランスフォーマーのバックボーンに直接投影することによってこうしたボトルネックを解消することを目指し、現代の推論駆動型フレームワークの舞台を整えました。
blocks.textEn: Earlier generations of models relied heavily on rigid cascaded pipelines where automatic speech recognition outputs fed directly into text-only LLMs. While straightforward to implement, this decoupled sequence suffered from catastrophic error propagation, where initial transcription mistakes permanently corrupted downstream reasoning. The transition to end-to-end multi-modal architectures sought to eliminate these bottlenecks by directly projecting acoustic features into the transformer backbone, setting the stage for modern reasoning-driven frameworks.

sections.heading: アーキテクチャのパラダイムとメカニスティックな革新

blocks.text: 現代の研究では、明確なアーキテクチャ上の革新とトレーニング戦略を通じて、中心的な表現のジレンマに取り組んでいます。例えば、FireRedAudioのような統合モデルは、単一の自己回帰型大規模言語モデル内に個別の連続入力表現を実装し、理解用の専用音声エンコーダーを活用する一方で、フローマッチング拡散トランスフォーマーを条件付ける再構築可能な経路を通じて音声生成をルーティングします。同時に、Continuous Audio Thinkingのようなフレームワークは、音声専門家からの蒸留を活用して推論プロセス全体を通じて重要な音響特性を維持する、内部の潜在ワークスペースを導入します。高密度な音声入力に伴う重い計算オーバーヘッドを管理するため、教師なしセグメンテーションや一様平均プーリングなどのトークン圧縮技術は、後段のデコーダーが消費する前に、入力トークン数を首尾よく削減します。これと並行して、空間音声統合手法は、Ambisonicsエンコーダーを利用して多チャンネル信号を回転対応特徴量にマッピングし、標準的なモノラルモデルを、一般的な理解パフォーマンスを犠牲にすることなく複数話者の帰属が可能な空間適格システムへと変革します。
blocks.textEn: Modern research tackles the core representation dilemma through distinct architectural innovations and training strategies. For instance, unified models like FireRedAudio implement separate continuous input representations within a single autoregressive large language model, utilizing a dedicated Audio Encoder for understanding while routing speech generation through a reconstructible pathway that conditions a flow-matching diffusion transformer. Simultaneously, frameworks like Continuous Audio Thinking introduce an internal latent workspace that leverages distillation from audio experts to retain critical acoustic properties throughout the reasoning process. To manage the heavy computational overhead associated with dense audio inputs, token compression techniques such as unsupervised segmentation and uniform average pooling successfully reduce input token counts before the downstream decoder consumes them. In parallel, spatial audio integration methods utilize Ambisonics encoders to map multi-channel signals into rotation-aware features, transforming standard monaural models into spatially competent systems capable of multi-speaker attribution without sacrificing general comprehension performance.

blocks.text: これらパラダイム全体の比較分析からは、計算効率と表現の粒度との間の明確なトレードオフが明らかになります。積極的なトークン圧縮はメモリフットプリントを大幅に削減し推論を高速化する一方で、正確なフォレンジック測位に必要な微細な音響トランジェントをならしてしまうリスクが偶発的に生じます。逆に、圧縮されていない潜在空間を維持することは豊富な教師信号を提供するものの、アクセラレータメモリに多大な負荷をかけるため、パラメータ効率の高い適応手法の採用が必要となります。
blocks.textEn: Comparative analysis across these paradigms reveals clear trade-offs between computational efficiency and representational granularity. While aggressive token compression significantly reduces memory footprints and accelerates inference, it occasionally risks smoothing over subtle acoustic transients required for precise forensic localization. Conversely, maintaining uncompressed latent spaces provides rich supervision signals but places heavy demands on accelerator memory, necessitating the adoption of parameter-efficient adaptation methods.

sections.heading: 内部メカニクス、アライメント、および検証

blocks.text: 高度な音声言語モデルが情報を処理し活用する方法を理解するには、内部表現のメカニズム、ポストトレーニングのアライメント戦略、そしてフォレンジック検証フレームワークという、3つの補完的な視点を検証する必要があります。メカニズムの観点から言えば、中間層のプロービングにより、音声による質問や概念が、モデルがトークンを出力するよりもずっと前に、言語に依存しない内部状態として明確になることが明らかになっており、通常のテキストキャプションではしばしば見落とされる超言語的ニュアンスや音響的感情をとらえています。デプロイの観点からは、グループ相対ポリシー最適化（GRPO）などの高度なポリシー最適化フレームワークにより、境界が客観的な音響的手がかりではなく主観的な編集上の判断に依存する自動メディアのチャプター化などの複雑な実務的タスクにモデルを適合させます。最後に、検証アプローチでは、偽装検知と時間的ローカライゼーションを共同で実行するためのフォレンジックを意識した推論データセットが導入され、モデルのハルシネーションを軽減し、高リスクなアプリケーション向けの説明可能性を高める明示的な証拠チェーンが確立されます。
blocks.textEn: Understanding how advanced audio language models process and utilize information requires examining three complementary perspectives: internal representation mechanics, post-training alignment strategies, and forensic verification frameworks. From a mechanistic standpoint, probing intermediate layers reveals that spoken questions and concepts become legible as language-agnostic internal states well before the model emits any tokens, capturing paralinguistic nuances and acoustic affect that standard text captions frequently discard. From a deployment perspective, advanced policy optimization frameworks such as Group Relative Policy Optimization align models with complex operational tasks like automated media chapterization, where boundaries rely on subjective editorial judgment rather than objective acoustic cues. Finally, verification approaches introduce forensic-aware reasoning datasets to jointly perform spoofing detection and temporal localization, establishing explicit evidence chains that mitigate model hallucinations and enhance interpretability for high-stakes applications.

blocks.text: これらの視点を統合することで、内部ワークスペースのプロービングと強化学習によるアライメントは孤立した技術ではなく、相互に補強し合う柱であることが示されます。プロービングは内部的決定がどこで行われるかについての診断的透明性を提供し、一方のポリシー最適化は、それらの内部表現を信頼性の高いタスク実行へと誘導するために構造化された報酬関数を活用します。
blocks.textEn: Synthesizing these viewpoints demonstrates that internal workspace probing and reinforcement learning alignment are not isolated techniques but mutually reinforcing pillars. Probing provides diagnostic transparency into where internal commitments occur, whereas policy optimization utilizes structured reward functions to steer those internal representations toward reliable task execution.

sections.heading: 評価の境界と解釈可能性のハードル

blocks.text: 顕著な構造的進歩にもかかわらず、音声AI研究全体において、特筆すべき評価の限界と説明可能性の課題が依然として存在しています。ブラックボックス生成により、実務者はモデルが特定の結論に至った理由を追跡することが極めて困難になっています。特に、微細な操作の手がかりが自然な音響的変動や録音のアーティファクトと容易に混同される可能性のある複雑なフォレンジックタスクにおいてはそれが顕著です。思考連鎖（チェーンオブソート）のモニタリングは、モデルが推論のステップを明示的に書き出す際に役立ちますが、中間表現の分析からは、隠れた処理が印刷されたトランスクリプトとは独立して動作することが多く、推論時に根拠のないハルシネーションの重大なリスクをもたらすことが示されています。さらに、現在の評価データセットは、制御された合成シミュレーションや、現実の音声ストリームが持つ多様性、ノイズ、予測不可能性を捉えきれない可能性のある作成者注釈付きのベンチマークに強く依存しています。したがって、研究者や実務者は、高いベンチマーク性能が敵対的環境や極めて主観的なデプロイ環境における堅牢な汎用性や信頼性を自動的に保証するわけではないことを認識し、これらの検証のギャップを慎重に乗り越えていかなければなりません。
blocks.textEn: Despite significant structural advancements, notable evaluation limits and interpretability challenges persist across audio AI research. Black-box generation makes it exceptionally difficult for practitioners to trace why a model arrives at specific conclusions, particularly in complex forensic tasks where subtle manipulation cues can easily be confused with natural acoustic variations or recording artifacts. While chain-of-thought monitoring helps when models explicitly write out their reasoning steps, intermediate representation analyses demonstrate that hidden processing often operates independently of printed transcripts, introducing severe risks of ungrounded hallucinations during inference. Furthermore, current evaluation datasets rely heavily on controlled synthetic simulations or creator-annotated benchmarks that may not capture the full diversity, noise, and unpredictability of wild audio streams. Researchers and practitioners must therefore navigate these validation gaps cautiously, recognizing that high benchmark performance does not automatically guarantee robust generalization or reliability in adversarial or highly subjective deployment environments.

blocks.text: 編集上のチャプター分けや音声の偽造箇所の特定といった主観的なタスクの評価は、現在の自動評価指標における深刻な限界をもたらすこともあります。標準的な重複度や精度のスコアは、人間の専門家が選択した代替的な境界配置の微妙な妥当性を捉えきれないことがよくあります。したがって、信頼性の高い評価スイートの開発は、洗練されたベンチマークのキュレーションと、専門家による人間の関与が不可欠な検証を必要とする、依然として未解決の課題となっています。
blocks.textEn: Evaluating subjective tasks like editorial chapterization or audio forgery localization also exposes deep limitations in current automatic metrics. Standard overlap or accuracy scores often fail to capture the nuanced validity of alternative boundary placements chosen by human experts. Developing reliable evaluation suites thus remains an open challenge requiring sophisticated benchmark curation and expert human-in-the-loop validation.

sections.heading: 実用上のインプリケーションと今後の研究方向性
sections.headingEn: Practical Implications and Future Research Directions

blocks.text: 研究者にとって、非結合型連続表現および明示的な推論監督への継続的な移行は、マルチモーダルアライメントや内部概念形成を研究するためのエキサイティングな新しい道を開くものです。補助的な監督が潜在的思考位置からテキスト出力へとどのように伝播するかを調査することは、多様なドメインにわたる汎用的な音声推論を改善するための主要な優先事項であり続けます。実務者にとって、これらの方法論的変化は、非構造化された音声アーカイブをナビゲート可能な構造化されたメディアストリームや信頼性の高いフォレンジック検証システムへと変革するための強力なツールを提供します。しかし、現実世界での展開を成功させるためには、積極的なトークン圧縮による計算上の制約の慎重なバランス調整と、アライメントの枠組みが主観的な人間の基準を明示的に考慮していることの確保に大きく依存します。これらの重大なトレードオフに対処することにより、音声言語モデルの将来の反復は、学術的ベンチマークのスコアと信頼できる商業的展開の間の永続的なギャップを首尾よく埋めることができます。
blocks.textEn: For researchers, the ongoing transition toward decoupled continuous representations and explicit reasoning supervision opens exciting new avenues for studying multimodal alignment and internal concept formation. Investigating how auxiliary supervision propagates from latent thinking positions to textual outputs will remain a central priority for improving generalizable audio reasoning across diverse domains. For practitioners, these methodological shifts offer powerful tools to transform unstructured audio archives into navigable, structured media streams and reliable forensic verification systems. However, successful real-world deployment will depend heavily on carefully balancing computational constraints through aggressive token compression and ensuring that alignment frameworks explicitly account for subjective human criteria. By addressing these critical trade-offs, future iterations of audio language models can successfully bridge the persistent gap between academic benchmark scores and dependable commercial deployment.

blocks.text: 分野が将来を見据える中で、空間認識、効率的なトークン削減、および強化学習に基づくアライメントの統合は、標準的な設計原則となる可能性が高いです。実務者は、これらのモデルを本番パイプラインに拡張する際に、トークンレートのトレードオフとアライメントのドリフトに警戒を怠らず、システムがあらゆる運用シナリオにおいて透明性のある検証可能なパフォーマンスを発揮するようにしなければなりません。
blocks.textEn: As the field looks ahead, the integration of spatial awareness, efficient token reduction, and reinforcement-guided alignment will likely become standard design principles. Practitioners must remain vigilant about token rate trade-offs and alignment drift when scaling these models to production pipelines, ensuring systems deliver transparent, verifiable performance across all operational scenarios.

sources.title: FireRedAudio: A General-Purpose Audio Language Model with Decoupled Continuous Representations for Understanding and Generation
sources.abstract: A unified audio model must recognize and understand linguistic, paralinguistic, and environmental information while supporting speech synthesis and editing. A key challenge is representation: understanding favors compact features suited to long-context modeling, whereas speech generation requires reconstructible features that preserve fine-grained acoustic detail. We introduce FireRedAudio, a general-purpose audio language model with a shared 9B-parameter LLM. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first publicly disclosed unified audio-language model to provide separate continuous input representations for understanding and generation within a single trainable autoregressive LLM. Audio to be recognized or analyzed is processed by a dedicated Audio Encoder, while speech inputs for generation use a RedAE-based pathway. The LLM directly generates text or conditions a flow-matching DiT to produce continuous acoustic latents. Through progressive multitask training, FireRedAudio supports ASR and audio understanding, with the latter extending to recordings of up to one hour, as well as zero-shot TTS, Instruct TTS, and semantic and acoustic speech editing. Its structured organization of long-form audio achieves second-level timestamp accuracy. Across comprehensive evaluations, FireRedAudio achieves competitive or leading performance in audio understanding and multilingual ASR, strong content accuracy and speaker preservation in zero-shot TTS, leading instruction following in Instruct TTS, and substantial improvements over Ming-UniAudio-Edit in both semantic and acoustic speech editing. These results demonstrate the viability of decoupled continuous input representations for unifying audio understanding and continuous-latent speech generation in a model of moderate scale. Our code is available at https://github.com/FireRedTeam/FireRedAudio.

sources.title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization
sources.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have made rapid progress on standardized benchmarks, yet their deployment in practical media workflows, curation, archival indexing, and content distribution remains largely unrealized. We identify automated audio chapterization, the task of segmenting continuous audio streams into thematically coherent chapters, as a demanding and commercially consequential setting that exposes this gap. Chapterization is challenging because boundaries are defined less by objective acoustic events than by subjective editorial judgment, requiring models to reason sequentially over long acoustic contexts and approximate creator-authored boundary decisions. We present AudioChaps, a post-training framework for aligning end-to-end LALMs for this task via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) guided by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. To support training and evaluation, we curate three datasets: AudioChaps-Alignment, derived from creator-annotated chapter boundaries on YouTube; AudioChaps-CoT, which provides structured supervision for well-formatted, high-quality, and evidence-grounded boundary reasoning; and AudioChaps-Eval, a held-out benchmark for audio chapterization. Applying GRPO directly without a Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) cold start, AudioChaps-R1-Zero already improves average F1 by 33 points over the state-of-the-art LALM Audio-Flamingo-3-Think. The AudioChaps framework produces our final aligned LALM, AudioChaps-R1, which improves average F1 by 49 points. These results demonstrate that GRPO-trained LALMs can reliably transform unstructured auditory streams into navigable, structured media. Our code, models, and dataset resources will be released upon acceptance at https://github.com/ta012/AudioChaps.

sources.title: Can We Read the Mind of an Audio LLM? A Verbalizable, Multilingual Middle-Layer Workspace
sources.abstract: An audio language model is a black box in a specific way: we see what it says, never what it works out on the way there, and chain-of-thought monitoring helps only if the model writes its reasoning down. Reading a base Qwen3-Omni with a logit lens at the audio-token positions, we find that the answer to a spoken question becomes legible - in words - in the model's middle layers, before it emits any token. Five findings follow. (1) The readout carries concepts in neither the question, the options, nor the model's own transcription: on a clip whose verbatim transcription is empty garbling, it reconstructs Watergate and scandal, passes through the role president, and resolves to Nixon - a hidden multi-hop chain, read with no chain-of-thought. (2) The content is language-agnostic: one audio-inferred concept surfaces in several scripts at once, and 38% of top-1 readouts are Chinese on English inputs. (3) It is paralinguistic: given the same clip as audio and as the model's own emotion-free caption, the audio mind forms the sound source, speaker role, or affect that the caption discards, and answers correctly more often. (4) The audio-driven signal is absent at the input, turns on about a tenth of the way into the network, separates most cleanly from the text prior in the middle band (35-80% of depth), and activation patching shows it is causally used and committed before the last fifth of the layers. (5) Deleting single layers maps the pipeline: reading the sound in is localized to the entry layers and answer delivery to the output layer, while retrieval is distributed across the interior. Throughout, a waveform-swap control - identical text, only the sound changed - isolates the audio-driven signal from a prior over the printed options. This is a qualitative account of what an audio model works out before it speaks: the quantities are controls, not benchmark scores.

sources.title: ThinkOmni: A Reasoning-Driven Omni-Modal LLM Framework for Audio Forgery Detection and Localization
sources.abstract: Existing audio forgery detection and localization (AFDL) methods often overfit dataset-specific low-level artifacts, limiting their generalization to subtle, localized, and unseen manipulations. Recent audio large language model (ALLM)-based approaches cast AFDL as question answering but still model forensic evidence implicitly, without linking manipulation cues to predictions. To bridge this gap, we propose ThinkOmni, a reasoning-driven omni-modal large language model that jointly performs explicit forensic reasoning, spoofing detection, and temporal manipulation localization. To enable explicit reasoning supervision, we construct Forensic-Aware Chain-of-Thought (FACoT), a 100K-sample dataset with structured forensic evidence and reasoning annotations. Leveraging FACoT, we introduce Forensic-Aware Modality-Incremental Learning (FMIL), which progressively aligns semantic, acoustic, and spectral-visual representations with the LLM backbone to capture complementary forensic cues. We further propose Forensic-Consistent Multi-task Loss (FCML), which combines weighted cross-entropy with an adaptive localization loss to coordinate reasoning generation, spoofing detection, and temporal localization. Extensive experiments show that ThinkOmni achieves strong cross-dataset generalization in both detection and localization. Code, models, data, and inference examples are available at https://beyond0814.github.io/ThinkOmni/.

sources.title: Continuous Audio Thinking for Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have shown impressive capabilities on diverse audio understanding tasks, ranging from speech transcription to music analysis. However, because LALMs are typically trained to produce text-aligned responses, their hidden states are progressively shaped for text generation rather than for preserving acoustic information. As a result, the diverse acoustic content that audio carries, such as phonetic detail, prosody, sound events, affect, and pitch, is lost along the way and difficult to leverage in the response. We introduce Continuous Audio Thinking (CoAT), a framework that equips audio language models with a continuous latent workspace for organizing acoustic information prior to response generation, grounded by distillation from audio experts. Within the thinking space, the model can utilize the rich acoustic information provided by expert distillation when generating its response. Furthermore, the proposed continuous thinking block can be processed in a single prefill, so CoAT does not require additional autoregressive decoding cost over the baseline. Across three LALMs, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, and Audio Flamingo~3, performance gains on a broad benchmark suite spanning audio reasoning, audio understanding, music classification, speech emotion, and speech transcription demonstrate the effectiveness of CoAT. Further analysis confirms that the auxiliary supervision propagates from the thinking positions to the model's textual responses.

sources.title: GAMA: A Large Audio-Language Model with Advanced Audio Understanding and Complex Reasoning Abilities
sources.abstract: Perceiving and understanding non-speech sounds and non-verbal speech is essential to making decisions that help us interact with our surroundings. In this paper, we propose GAMA, a novel General-purpose Large Audio-Language Model (LALM) with Advanced Audio Understanding and Complex Reasoning Abilities. We build GAMA by integrating an LLM with multiple types of audio representations, including features from a custom Audio Q-Former, a multi-layer aggregator that aggregates features from multiple layers of an audio encoder. We fine-tune GAMA on a large-scale audio-language dataset, which augments it with audio understanding capabilities. Next, we propose CompA-R (Instruction-Tuning for Complex Audio Reasoning), a synthetically generated instruction-tuning (IT) dataset with instructions that require the model to perform complex reasoning on the input audio. We instruction-tune GAMA with CompA-R to endow it with complex reasoning abilities, where we further add a soft prompt as input with high-level semantic evidence by leveraging event tags of the input audio. Finally, we also propose CompA-R-test, a human-labeled evaluation dataset for evaluating the capabilities of LALMs on open-ended audio question-answering that requires complex reasoning. Through automated and expert human evaluations, we show that GAMA outperforms all other LALMs in literature on diverse audio understanding tasks by margins of 1%-84%. Further, GAMA IT-ed on CompA-R proves to be superior in its complex reasoning and instruction following capabilities.

sources.title: Towards Audio Token Compression in Large Audio Language Models
sources.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) deliver strong performance across speech and audio tasks, but their audio encoders generate high-rate token sequences (e.g., 25 tokens/s), making attention computation costly and limiting scalability. In this paper, we explore techniques such as unsupervised segmentation, uniform average pooling, etc., to reduce the number of audio tokens before they are consumed by the LLM decoder. To mitigate potential performance degradation, we employ low-rank adapters during finetuning. We evaluate our proposed models on two tasks, automatic speech recognition and speech-to-speech translation tasks, that are dependent on effectively uncovering the underlying lexical content of the input signal, and study the effect of downsampling on these tasks. Experimental results show that compressed LALMs can achieve performance closer to frame-level LALMs while reducing the input audio token count up to three times before the LLM backbone.

sources.title: SPUR: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Integrating Spatial Audio Understanding and Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models
sources.abstract: Spatial perception is central to auditory intelligence, enabling accurate understanding of real-world acoustic scenes and advancing human-level perception of the world around us. While recent large audio-language models (LALMs) show strong reasoning over complex audios, most operate on monaural inputs and lack the ability to capture spatial cues such as direction, elevation, and distance. We introduce SPUR, a lightweight, plug-in approach that equips LALMs with spatial perception through minimal architectural changes. SPUR consists of: (i) a First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) encoder that maps (W, X, Y, Z) channels to rotation-aware, listener-centric spatial features, integrated into target LALMs via a multimodal adapter; and (ii) SPUR-Set, a spatial QA dataset combining open-source FOA recordings with controlled simulations, emphasizing relative direction, elevation, distance, and overlap for supervised spatial reasoning. Fine-tuning our model on the SPUR-Set consistently improves spatial QA and multi-speaker attribution while preserving general audio understanding. SPUR provides a simple recipe that transforms monaural LALMs into spatially aware models. Extensive ablations validate the effectiveness of our approach.
